Source: http://www.kubby.com/AMMA.html

Posted January 21, 2000

From Steve Kubby

THE AMERICAN MEDICAL MARIJUANA ASSOCIATION
Monarch Bay Plaza, Box 375, Dana Point, Ca 92629
See
On 1st Anniversary Of His Arrest Steve Kubby Notes Plight Of Other Medical Marijuana Patients

1-21-00
Dear Friends,

Dr. Sinkosky and the Metropolitan Detention Center are breaking the law and violating the civil and medical rights of Todd McCormick.

The Compassionate Use Act IS the LAW, and it is illegal NOT to OBEY it AND it cannot be changed, except by a new election vote, or a successful challenge in appellate court. The drug warriors know that they can't muster the votes and they can't win in court, so they've deliberately engaged in a program of disinformation to deceive and frighten citizens away from asserting their newly created medical rights:

The California Constitution Article 2 Section 10 states that Prop. 215 legally became the law of California the day after the 1996 election and that only the voters can amend or repeal the Compassionate Use Act now that it has passed:

(a) An initiative statute or referendum approved by a majority of votes thereon TAKES EFFECT THE DAY AFTER THE ELECTION unless the measure provides otherwise. [emphasis added]

(c) The Legislature. . .may amend or repeal an initiative statute by another statute that becomes effective ONLY WHEN APPROVED BY THE ELECTORS unless the initiative statute permits amendment or repeal without their approval.
[emphasis added]

So, to sum up the legal argument:

-ANY law passed by the voters of California becomes a law the next day.

-California laws that conflict with federal laws MUST legally be obeyed until successfully challenged in appellate court.

-NO law passed by the voters may be modified or limited by anyone, even the legislature, UNLESS approved by a majority vote of the electors.

Furthermore, because Todd is disabled, they are violating his federal rights under the ADA which makes it a crime to threaten or deprive a disabled person of " ANY rights guaranteed under state law. " Under the Bane Act and other hate-crime legislation, officials and officers who violate disabled rights under state law, are to be punished with " enhanced " sentences of longer periods.

The Bane Civil Rights Act protects people from continued violence or the threat of violence based on grounds such as race, color, religion, ancestry, national origin, political affiliation, sex, sexual orientation, age, disability or position in a labor dispute. It also punishes persons responsible for such violence. If you believe you have a claim under this Act, you may wish to file a private lawsuit. The court may grant an injunction prohibiting further intimidating or coercive behavior against Todd. Any violation of this order is a misdemeanor and may result in fines or imprisonment. If a judgment is awarded in your favor in a private lawsuit, you may receive reasonable attorneys fees as well.

GRAND JURIES have the power to investigate and act on this matter. In fact, the grand jury has the power to remove district attorneys and sheriffs from office! The powers and duties of the grand jury in connection with proceedings for the removal of district, county, or city officers are prescribed in Article 3 (commencing with Section 3060), Chapter 7,
Division 4, Title 1, of the Government Code.

I've been spending all my time lately presenting evidence and arguments to the Placer and Orange County Grand Juries. The grand jury folks, who are ordinary citizens, are absolutely GREAT to work with. Everyone has been cooperative and helpful as we put together these two massive indictments of Lungren, Gates and their associates. The media may be ignoring us, but the wheels of justice are in motion and there is nothing that will stop it now.

I don't live in LA County and I don't have a direct interest in this matter, so I can't file a complaint myself. However, I urge those involved in Todd's terrible plight to file a complaint immediately with the LA Grand Jury.

Furthermore, I will be happy to volunteer my services if needed.

Take back you power!

Steve

From Tod H. Mikuriya, M.D.
1168 Sterling Avenue
Berkeley, CA 94708-1757
mikuriya@igc.org
http://www.mikuriya.com/althealth

January 20, 2000

Metropolitan Detention Center
535 North Alameda Street
Los Angeles, CA 90012

Re: Todd McCormick DoB 10-07-70

To whom it may concern:

I have attempted to continue my treatment of the above-captioned with prescriptions of Marinol which he finds useful in managing his pain and muscle spasms in his neck and upper back.

On January 11 in response to a request from his friend I spoke briefly with Dr. Sinkosky (sp?) shortly after 6 AM when I was directed to call by the ward nurse the previous afternoon. I attempted to discuss his case but all I was able to say was Todd McCormick and Marinol. " I can't talk to you. I don't know who you are. " and referred me to the facility attorney. No attempt was made to verify. This response was inappropriate and beneath usual community standards of medical practice. My good faith-attempt at collegial communication to get proper treatment for my patient was thwarted. This will result in avoidable pain, muscle spasm, anorexia and cachexia.

Tod H. Mikuriya, M.D.
